title: Rehabilitation Robotics
summary: Wearable and stationary robotic systems for trunk, spine, upper-limb, and hand rehabilitation.
questions: How can rehabilitation robots deliver effective physical support while preserving active participation and natural movement?

title: Intelligent Robot Control
summary: Adaptive and compliant control strategies that coordinate robot assistance with human movement and rehabilitation needs.
questions: How can a robot remain responsive and stable while adapting to a patient's changing capabilities?

title: Biomechanical Analysis
summary: Robot-assisted assessment and quantitative analysis of trunk control, movement function, and human–robot coordination.
questions: Which biomechanical measures can characterize motor impairment and rehabilitation progress?

title: Variable-Stiffness Mechanisms
summary: High-compatibility mechanisms and control methods that tune stiffness for safe, efficient, and comfortable assistance.
questions: How can variable stiffness improve compatibility and dynamic compliance in wearable rehabilitation robots?

title: Clinical Translation
summary: Translation of rehabilitation robotics from engineering prototypes to patient studies and clinically meaningful assessment.
questions: How can robotic technologies be evaluated safely and meaningfully with patients in real rehabilitation settings?
